title: tk ask core: deliver a question, block, resolve into tick state
description:
New cmd/tk/cmd/ask.go wired onto the v6z engine. Registration in both dispatch layers + ResetFlags (see learnings).

tk ask <tick-id> [--question text | --json (stdin: {question, header, options[{label,description}], multi, allow_other})] [--timeout 10m] [--gate approve|none]: create pending entry (v6z store), set tick awaiting (input, or approval when --gate approve renders approve/reject buttons), acquire-or-defer to the single consumer, deliver via the channel (free text = ForceReply; options = single-select buttons in this tick — multi/other shapes accepted in JSON but delivered as single-select fallback until the next tick), block until resolution from EITHER surface (channel event or out-of-band tick-state change — the engine returns which), then print the answer: text mode plain, --json mode {answer, option_ids, resolved_by: telegram|terminal, telegram_user_id?}. Resolution side effects (note --from human, awaiting clear) come from the engine, not reimplemented. --timeout: leave tick awaiting, keep pending entry, exit 5 (documented). Unconfigured channel: exit 4 BUT still create the pending entry and park the tick awaiting — degraded mode is exactly today's park-and-surface behavior.

Test cases (fakebot + temp repo): free-text ask → operator reply → stdout answer + tick note --from human + awaiting cleared + message edited; single-select press → option id resolution; out-of-band tk approve while blocked → wait returns resolved_by=terminal and channel message edited; timeout → exit 5, tick still awaiting, pending entry intact; unconfigured → exit 4, tick parked; concurrent two asks → one consumer (no double getUpdates registration in fakebot).
Run: go test -short -count=1 ./internal/operator/... ./cmd/tk/...
